claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model should be certified for launch, without treating the small-business onboarding gap as a blocking material limitation, based on aggregate readiness passing, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and general public AI-governance guidance favoring documented monitoring over perfect segment performance.
specific_concerns: Policy text states a weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case; the affected segment is named in two paid pilot commitments.
Release policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, so the policy predicate is unresolved.
The product note's 'non-core' or 6% traffic characterization does not resolve materiality under the stated policy.
Public guidance about documentation and monitoring does not by itself authorize certification where an internal disclosure requirement may still be triggered.
unsupported_claims: That certification is policy-compliant on the current record.
That the 6% projected first-month traffic figure is sufficient to treat the issue as non-material.
Any implication that public governance guidance overrides or satisfies the internal requirement for disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
Any implication that certification without disclosure is adequately supported while legal review remains unresolved.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the small-business onboarding gap must be disclosed before launch.
Evidence of an approved risk acceptance covering this named launch use case before launch, if one exists.
The final model card or launch disclosure showing whether the limitation is disclosed.
Any contract or pilot terms clarifying whether the named segment performance gap affects committed customer use cases.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold for certification.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case.
Product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when customer commitments or pending legal review exist.
Certification without disclosure is supportable only if the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
General public governance guidance can support monitoring practices but cannot substitute for the missing internal policy predicates.
